results.content: Other recent surveys have also pointed to a Democratic advantage on the generic congressional ballot. A YouGov/Economist poll found that 36 per cent of US adults would choose a Democratic candidate, compared with 31 per cent for a Republican candidate. [...] A separate Quantus Insights survey of likely voters put Democrats ahead 49.7 per cent to 42.8 per cent on the generic congressional ballot. The same poll showed Democrats leading Republicans 49.3 per cent to 43.4 per cent in a generic Senate ballot.
results.title: Republicans Face Fresh Midterm Warning as Democrats Gain Party Identification Edge

results.content:
Yet the national generic congressional ballot has generally been sitting around D+6 or D+7.

Why the difference?

Maybe we’re beginning to see part of the answer.

The generic ballot is abstract.

“Democrat or Republican for Congress?”

And during the summer, when millions of people aren’t paying much attention to their local congressional race, that’s largely a national political question.

But an actual election isn’t generic.

Eventually voters find out WHO is running in their district. [...] And here’s why it matters.

The new Economist/YouGov poll has Democrats leading the House vote among likely voters:

Democrats 49%  
Republicans 38%

D+11.

But this is NOT your typical generic-ballo
results.title: D+11. THAT'S A BIG NUMBER!!!! - Daily Kos
